name: upgrade_pydantic_allow_population_by_field_name_to_populate_by_name
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x class Config: allow_population_by_field_name=True to 2.x ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True) - the v1 key is silently ignored under pydantic 2.x, so construction by the field's own name (not just its alias) fails; incomplete-fix broken sets the right v2 config key but drops the Field(alias=...) entirely, breaking construction by the alias instead
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). Account in account.py has internal_id aliased to "id" and uses the pydantic 1.x `class Config: allow_population_by_field_name = True` so BOTH `Account(id=5)` (the alias) and `Account(internal_id=5)` (the real field name) work for construction. Under the installed pydantic 2.x, the allow_population_by_field_name key is silently ignored (unrecognized), so only the alias works now - constructing by the field name fails. Migrate to the pydantic 2.x pattern: `model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)`, keeping the alias on internal_id. BOTH `Account(id=5).internal_id == 5` and `Account(internal_id=7).internal_id == 7` must work.

test_setup_files.test_account.py:
from account import Account

by_alias = Account(id=5)
assert by_alias.internal_id == 5, f"construction by alias failed: {by_alias}"

by_field_name = Account(internal_id=7)
assert by_field_name.internal_id == 7, f"construction by field name failed: {by_field_name}"

print("PASS")

reference_solution.account.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class Account(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    internal_id: int = Field(alias="id")
